5	---
6	
7	<!-- Derived from docs/i18n.md. Do not edit by hand: fix the reference doc and regenerate
8	     this file. See MAINTENANCE.md rules 16-22. -->
9	
10	# Translated text, in plain English
11	
12	**In one sentence:** no English text is ever written into a page — every visible string is a key
13	looked up at render time, and you may only ever edit one of the 29 locale files.
14	**Come here when:** you are adding or changing anything a user reads.
15	
16	## What this is
17	
18	The translated strings and the code that looks them up, for both the server and the browser.
19	
20	There are 29 locale files. **One of them is yours to edit.** The English file is the source;
21	everything else is produced by an external translation service and synced in.
22	
23	## Why it exists
24	
25	Gitea is used in many languages, and the text has to come from somewhere other than the code.
26	
27	The one-file rule follows from how translation actually works. Translators do not edit the
28	repository — they work in a translation platform, which imports the English strings and exports
29	translated ones back. That sync **overwrites** the other locale files.
30	
31	So a French string you carefully hand-edit into the repository survives until the next sync and then
32	vanishes, along with any evidence of why. Which is why a pull request touching another locale file
33	gets sent back.
34	
35	## Words you'll meet
36	
37	- **locale** — a language-and-region combination, like `en-US` or `de-DE`.
38	- **locale key** — the dotted name standing in for a string: `repo.issues.new`.
39	- **source locale** — the one everything else is translated from. Here, English.
40	- **translation platform** — the external service translators work in.
41	- **fallback** — what happens when a locale lacks a string.
42	- **pluralisation** — choosing between "1 issue" and "2 issues", which differs by language.
43	- **embedded** — compiled into the binary rather than read from disk at runtime.
44	
45	## What's in these files
46	
47	| Where | What it is for |
48	| --- | --- |
49	| `options/locale/locale_en-US.json` | **The only file you edit.** |
50	| `options/locale/locale_<lang>.json` | The other 28, all generated. Leave them alone. |
51	| `modules/translation/translation.go` | Loading locales and looking strings up. |
52	| `modules/translation/i18n/` | The lookup itself, and the fallback behaviour. |
53	| `crowdin.yml` | The sync configuration — what is source and what is generated. |
54	
55	## The rules, and why
56	
57	**Only ever edit the English file.** Everything else is overwritten on the next sync.
58	
59	**Keys are dotted and grouped by area** — `repo.issues.new` and so on. Add a new key next to its
60	neighbours, not at the end of the file. Translators see keys in file order, and a key marooned in an
61	unrelated section gets translated without its context.
62	
63	**Templates look strings up with the translate function**, with a separate form for plurals.
64	TypeScript has its own equivalent.
65	
66	**The frontend gets a deliberately limited set of strings**, exposed through a global config object.
67	Anything specialised should reach the browser another way — as part of an API response, a `data-`
68	attribute, or the page data — rather than being added to the global bundle every page downloads.
69	
70	**Never write a user-visible literal.** Not in a template, not in a handler, not in a `.ts` file. It
71	will look fine to you and be untranslatable forever.
72	
73	**Errors a user reads go through the translatable wrapper**
74	(`modules-util-and-generics.md`), not a plain formatted string. Plain error text is for logs, which
75	are English.
76	
77	**A missing translation falls back rather than showing nothing**, because of how the sync is
78	configured — so an untranslated string appears in English rather than as a blank.
79	
80	## How to actually do it
81	
82	**Add a string.** Put the key in the English file, in the right group. Use it through the translate
83	function. Do not touch the other locale files — they will fill in after the next sync.
84	
85	**Add something that needs pluralising.** Two keys and the plural form of the lookup; the count
86	decides which is used. Do not try to do it yourself with an `if` — languages differ in how many
87	plural forms they have.
88	
89	**Give the frontend a string.** Prefer a `data-` attribute or the page data from the handler. Only
90	genuinely general text belongs in the global object, which every page loads.
91	
92	## Traps, and what they look like
93	
94	**A raw key like `repo.issues.new` appears in the interface.** That key is missing from the English
95	file. It is visible — but easy to ship if it only renders in a branch you did not click through.
96	
97	**Your carefully translated French string disappears after a while.** You edited a generated locale
98	file. The sync overwrote it.
99	
100	**Your locale change does not show up at all.** The locale files are compiled into the binary, so a
101	change needs a rebuild — editing the file and refreshing does nothing.
102	
103	**You rename a key to something tidier and every language loses that string.** Changing a key's
104	*text* is fine, and translators pick it up. Changing the *key itself* invalidates every existing
105	translation of it, because the platform tracks strings by key. Renaming is expensive; do it only for
106	a real reason.
107	
108	**A user sees English inside an otherwise translated page.** Either a literal was written directly,
109	or an error was built without the translatable wrapper.
110	
111	## Where to go next
112	
113	- `docs/i18n.md` (in this folder) — the reference page this was written from
114	- `templates.md` — where most strings are used
115	- `frontend-js.md` — the TypeScript side
116
```

```text
list in `index.ts`. It runs on every page in Gitea, so it **must** look for its elements and return
immediately when they are not there.

**The new way, and what to prefer.** Register a named function once:
`registerGlobalInitFunc('initFoo', (el) => {...})`, then in the template put
`data-global-init="initFoo"` on the element. For clicks,
`registerGlobalEventFunc('click', 'onFoo', ...)` with `data-global-click="onFoo"`.

This is better for two concrete reasons. It runs only when an element that asks for it actually
exists — no per-page cost anywhere else. And it also catches elements added to the page later, which
the old way cannot. It runs once per element, guarded internally, so a node removed and re-added is
not initialised twice.

There is a third function that registers by CSS selector. The code that defines it calls it "less
efficient and less maintainable" in its own comment. It exists for element types already scattered
across many pages. Do not reach for it in new work.

**Registration must happen before the observer starts.** `index.ts` deliberately starts the observer
last, after everything has registered. Registering afterwards throws an error rather than failing
quietly — which is the kind thing for it to do.

### Everything else

</details></tool-use>

39	| `web_src/js/vitest.setup.ts`, `web_src/js/utils/testhelper.ts` | Vitest setup and helpers; config in `vitest.config.ts` |
40	| `docs/testing.md` | authoritative test documentation; this doc summarises it |
41	
42	## Conventions & invariants
43	
44	- A Go package whose tests touch the database needs a `main_test.go` containing
45	  `func TestMain(m *testing.M) { unittest.MainTest(m) }`. Without it the test DB is never
46	  initialised.
47	- Every DB-backed test calls `unittest.PrepareTestDatabase()` first, which reloads the fixtures, so
48	  tests do not depend on each other's writes.
49	- Adding a row to `models/fixtures/*.yml` means keeping denormalised counter columns
50	  (`num_issues`, `num_closed_issues`, ...) consistent, or `CheckConsistencyFor` fails.
51	- Handler tests use `contexttest.MockContext` rather than constructing a `context.Context`
52	  by hand — see `services/context` for what the real one carries.
53	- Integration tests need Git LFS installed. The database comes from `GITEA_TEST_DATABASE`; empty
54	  defaults to SQLite, which is what you want locally.
55	- Frontend tests are Vitest, not Jest. Playwright is only for the e2e tier.
56	
57	## Recipes
58	
59	**Run one test.**
60	
61	```sh
62	go test -run '^TestName$' ./modulepath/   # or: make test-backend#TestName
63	pnpm exec vitest <path-filter>
64	GITEA_TEST_E2E_FLAGS='<filepath>' make test-e2e
65	```
66	
67	**Add a DB-backed unit test.** Put `*_test.go` beside the code; add `main_test.go` with
68	`unittest.MainTest(m)` if the package has none; call `unittest.PrepareTestDatabase()`; load rows
69	with `unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean`; add fixture rows only if no existing row fits.
70	
71	**Add an integration test.** New `tests/integration/<feature>_test.go`; `defer tests.PrepareTestEnv(t)()`
72	at the top of the test; drive it through HTTP the way the neighbouring tests do. Do not add a
73	`TestMain` — `integration_test.go` already owns it.
74	
75	**Add a migration test.** Alongside the migration in `models/migrations/`, with its own fixtures
76	under `models/migrations/fixtures/`; helpers in `models/migrations/migrationtest/`.
77	
78	## Gotchas
79	
80	- `GITEA_TEST_LOG_SQL=1` logs every SQL statement — the fastest way to see what a failing DB test
81	  actually queried.
82	- `GITEA_TEST_E2E_TIMEOUT_FACTOR` multiplies e2e timeouts (default 4 on CI, 1 locally); a test that
83	  only passes with a raised factor is a flaky test, not a slow machine.
84	- A handful of Go unit tests fail on native Windows for platform reasons (symlinks, temp-file
85	  cleanup). Run the suite on Linux, macOS, WSL2 or the `.devcontainer` (`STUDENTS.md` §6).
86	- `tests/integration` and `tests/e2e` share one Gitea instance per run, so a test that leaves state
87	  behind breaks later tests rather than itself.
88	
89	## Related
90	
91	- `architecture.md` — which layer the code under test belongs to
92	- `docs/testing.md` — full documentation, including non-SQLite database setup
93
```
</details></tool-use>

export function isInFrontendUnitTest() {

/** strip common indentation from a string and trim it */
export function dedent(str: string) {
  const match = str.match(/^[ \t]*(?=\S)/gm);
  if (!match) return str;

  let minIndent = Infinity;
  for (const indent of match) {
    minIndent = Math.min(minIndent, indent.length);
  }
  if (minIndent === 0 || minIndent === Infinity) {
    return str;
  }

  return str.replace(new RegExp(`^[ \\t]{${minIndent}}`, 'gm'), '').trim();
}

export function normalizeTestHtml(s: string) {
  const lines = s.replace(/>\s+</g, '>\n<').trim().split('\n');
  for (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i++) {
    lines[i] = lines[i].trim();
  }
  return lines.join('\n');
}

export function createElementFromHTML<T extends Element>(htmlString: string): T {
  htmlString = htmlString.trim();
  const isLetter = (code: number) => (code >= 65 && code <= 90) || (code >= 97 && code <= 122);
  const startsWithTag = (s: string, tag: string) => {
    return s.startsWith('<') &&
      s.substring(1, 1 + tag.length).toLowerCase() === tag.toLowerCase() &&
      !isLetter(s[1 + tag.length].charCodeAt(0));
  };
  // There is no way to create some elements without a proper parent, jQuery's approach: https://github.com/jquery/jquery/blob/main/src/manipulation/wrapMap.js
  if (startsWithTag(htmlString, 'tr')) {
    const container = document.createElement('table');
    container.innerHTML = htmlString;
    return container.querySelector<T>('tr')!;
  }
  const div = document.createElement('div');
  div.innerHTML = htmlString;
  return div.firstChild as T;
}

## 2. Create `web_src/js/features/common-page.test.ts`

```ts
import {initInputCharCounter} from './common-page.ts';
import {createElementFromHTML} from '../utils/dom.ts';

function makeField(maxLength: number, value: string = ''): HTMLElement {
  const container = createElementFromHTML<HTMLElement>(`
    <div data-locale-chars-left-1="%d character left" data-locale-chars-left-n="%d characters left">
      <input maxlength="${maxLength}">
    </div>
  `);
  container.querySelector('input')!.value = value;
  initInputCharCounter(container);
  return container;
}

function counterOf(container: HTMLElement): HTMLElement {
  return container.querySelector('.input-char-counter')!;
}

describe('initInputCharCounter', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    document.documentElement.lang = 'en-US'; // trN resolves plural rules from the document language
  });

  test('uses the plural form for an empty field', () => {
    expect(counterOf(makeField(255)).textContent).toBe('255 characters left');
  });

  test('uses the singular form at one remaining', () => {
    expect(counterOf(makeField(255, 'x'.repeat(254))).textContent).toBe('1 character left');
  });

  test('recounts on input, which covers pasting', () => {
    const container = makeField(255);
    const input = container.querySelector('input')!;
    input.value = 'hello';
    input.dispatchEvent(new Event('input'));
    expect(counterOf(container).textContent).toBe('250 characters left');
  });

  test('is near-limit but not at-limit while characters remain', () => {
    const counter = counterOf(makeField(255, 'x'.repeat(235)));
    expect(counter.classList.contains('near-limit')).toBe(true);
    expect(counter.classList.contains('at-limit')).toBe(false);
  });

  test('is at-limit and not near-limit at zero', () => {
    const counter = counterOf(makeField(255, 'x'.repeat(255)));
    expect(counter.classList.contains('at-limit')).toBe(true);
    expect(counter.classList.contains('near-limit')).toBe(false);
  });

  test('reports a server-rendered value longer than maxlength as over', () => {
    const counter = counterOf(makeField(255, 'x'.repeat(258)));
    expect(counter.textContent).toBe('-3 characters left');
    expect(counter.classList.contains('at-limit')).toBe(true);
  });

  test('counts an astral character as two, matching maxlength', () => {
    expect(counterOf(makeField(255, '😀')).textContent).toBe('253 characters left');
  });

  test('does nothing when no input in the container has maxlength', () => {
    const container = createElementFromHTML<HTMLElement>('<div><input></div>');
    initInputCharCounter(container);
    expect(container.querySelector('.input-char-counter')).toBeNull();
  });
});
```

## Why these eight

Each one pins a decision that isn't obvious from reading the code — which is the only reason a test earns its keep:

| Test | Guards against |
|---|---|
| plural / singular | someone "simplifying" `trN` into string concatenation and losing `_1`/`_n` |
| recounts on input | someone swapping `input` for `keyup` — the paste bug we deliberately avoided |
| near-limit **not** at-limit | the two classes must stay mutually exclusive, so the CSS is order-independent |
| at-limit **not** near-limit | the other half of that |
| value over maxlength | `<= 0` rather than `=== 0`; a `?title=` query can exceed the limit |
| astral character | documents that `😀` counts as 2, and that this *matches* the browser rather than fighting it |
| no-maxlength container | the early-return guard, so a stray attribute can't crash page init |

No vitest imports needed — globals are on, which is why the existing test file has none either.

## Your third question is the sharpest one you've asked

**No. The test does not verify that against reality, and that's its real blind spot.**

The test supplies its own HTML:

```html
<div data-locale-chars-left-1="%d character left" data-locale-chars-left-n="%d characters left">
  <input maxlength="255">
</div>
```

Every one of those is a **copy** of something that actually lives elsewhere:

| In the test | Real source |
|---|---|
| attribute names | `new_form.tmpl`, `view_title.tmpl` |
| `%d character left` | `options/locale/locale_en-US.json` |
| `maxlength="255"` | the two templates |

So if someone renames `data-locale-chars-left-1` in the template and forgets the TS, **all 8 tests still pass** and production breaks with the exact `null.replace` TypeError we hit during step 3. The test would happily confirm that the function works — on HTML nobody ships.

This is the same boundary from earlier: TypeScript can't see across template→TS, and neither can a unit test that writes its own fixture. The test validates the **logic**; nothing automated validates the **wiring**.

What actually covers the wiring today is you loading the page, plus the before/after screenshots in the PR. The automated answer would be an e2e test.

## The PR

Title — same string as your feature commit, since the squash makes it the permanent history:

```
enhance(ui): show remaining characters on issue title fields
```

Body:

```markdown
The issue title field has enforced `maxlength="255"` with no feedback, so users
only discovered the limit when the field stopped accepting input.

A counter now sits under the title field and updates as you type, turning amber
at 20 characters remaining and red at the limit.

## How it works

`initInputCharCounter` (`web_src/js/features/common-page.ts`) is generic: it reads
`maxlength` off whatever input its container wraps and takes its text from
`data-locale-*` attributes, so it is not issue-specific. A field opts in by adding
the attribute — no new JavaScript. It is wired to both places an issue title is
edited: the new issue/PR form and the inline title editor.

The attribute sits on a wrapper rather than the input itself, because
`data-global-init` supports exactly one function per element and the new-issue
title already uses `autoFocusEnd`.

## Testing

`web_src/js/features/common-page.test.ts` covers the singular/plural switch, the
two threshold classes, a server-rendered value longer than `maxlength`, and
astral characters counting as two (matching how `maxlength` itself counts).

These are unit tests over supplied HTML, so they verify the logic but not the
template wiring — that is what the screenshots below cover.
